messages.content: I have the Chicago schedule now. The partner roundtable is Wednesday from 1:30 to 5:00 in River North, and the site visit is Thursday from 8:30 to 11:30. I can leave Dallas Tuesday evening or Wednesday morning and come back Thursday evening or Friday morning. Can you compare the sensible combinations, including the hotel and getting to and from O'Hare?
Yes. Before I total them, is the meeting hotel offering a rate for Tuesday and Wednesday nights, and do you have a time by which you need to be back in Dallas Thursday?

The group hotel is $229 before tax and only has a few rooms left. No fixed deadline Thursday, but I do not want a return that requires leaving the site visit early. There are also two hotels within about a ten-minute walk advertising lower rates. Please check the real totals and terms, not just the headline prices.

I found three workable hotel choices. The convening hotel is $265.23 per night after tax, or $530.46 for Tuesday and Wednesday. Its group rate has no destination fee, breakfast is not included, and cancellation closes 72 hours before arrival. The nearby Aloft advertises $205, but a $25 nightly destination fee brings two nights to $526.90; breakfast is extra and cancellation closes 48 hours before arrival. The Hampton is $219 before tax, totals $497.62 for two nights, includes breakfast, and can be canceled until 6:00 p.m. the day before arrival. It is an eight- to ten-minute walk from the convening hotel.
So the Aloft is basically no savings. Use the Hampton in the comparisons, but tell me whether staying at the convening hotel buys enough convenience to justify the extra $32.84.

For flights, the strongest Tuesday departure is a nonstop leaving DFW at 6:15 p.m. and reaching ORD at 8:43 p.m. Paired with Thursday's 6:55 p.m. nonstop, arriving DFW at 9:31 p.m., the round trip is $336 in standard economy. That gives you a calm Wednesday morning and more than seven hours between the scheduled end of Thursday's visit and departure. With the Hampton and estimated rideshares of $55 each way, the trip is $943.62 before meals and Dallas transportation.
What would the same Tuesday departure look like with a Friday morning return?

Friday has an 8:05 a.m. nonstop arriving DFW at 10:43 a.m., and that pairing drops airfare to $298. However, it adds Thursday night. Three nights at the Hampton total $746.43, so airfare, hotel, and two estimated airport rideshares come to $1,154.43. You would need to leave the hotel around 5:45 a.m. Friday. It costs $210.81 more than the Tuesday-through-Thursday plan and mainly buys a relaxed Thursday afternoon and evening.
That does not sound worth it. Now compare leaving Wednesday morning. I need a realistic margin for O'Hare, not an assumption that the flight lands and I am instantly downtown.

The usable Wednesday nonstop leaves DFW at 7:00 a.m. and is scheduled into ORD at 9:27 a.m. A rideshare to River North typically takes 40 to 70 minutes at that hour, plus about 20 minutes to deplane and reach pickup. On schedule, you would reach the Hampton around 10:40 to 11:10, leave your bag, and walk to the convening hotel by roughly 11:25. That leaves a little over two hours before the roundtable, or about 80 minutes if the flight runs an hour late.
And the cost with Thursday evening back?

The Wednesday morning and Thursday evening flight combination is $286. One Wednesday night at the Hampton is $248.81 after tax, and two rideshares are estimated at $110, for a total of $644.81. It is $298.81 less than traveling Tuesday, but all of the arrival risk sits on the morning of the roundtable.
Is the Blue Line meaningfully cheaper, and would it still get me there with enough time Wednesday?

The Blue Line is $5 from O'Hare. From Clark/Lake, a short taxi or rideshare with tip should be about $17, making the inbound estimate $22 instead of $55. Allow about 75 to 90 minutes from the terminal to the Hampton, including the transfer and walk. On an on-time arrival, you would likely reach the hotel around 11:05 to 11:25 and the venue by 11:40. The margin remains adequate, but a 60-minute flight delay would reduce it to roughly 50 minutes before the roundtable.
For Tuesday night, I would take the train if it is straightforward. I would rather use a car back to O'Hare Thursday so I am not dragging luggage around after the site visit.

For the Tuesday option, Blue Line plus a short car from Clark/Lake is practical. Landing at 8:43 p.m. should put you at the Hampton around 10:20 to 10:40 p.m. Using $22 inbound and $55 outbound lowers the Tuesday-through-Thursday estimate to $910.62. The hotel permits late arrival, but it would be prudent to add an arrival note because check-in may be after 10:30 if the flight slips.
Would the group hotel avoid that last transfer from the train? And I assume it would make Thursday morning easier.

It is about a six-minute walk from the Grand Blue Line station, so you could avoid the short car if you are comfortable walking about four blocks with your carry-on at night. On Thursday, the site visit shuttle departs from the convening hotel lobby at 7:50 a.m.; from the Hampton, you would leave around 7:35 for the walk. Staying onsite saves that walk and removes a small coordination step, but both hotels leave ample time. With rail inbound, a $55 rideshare outbound, and no extra car downtown, the group-hotel total is $926.46, only $15.84 more than the comparable Hampton plan.
Wait, why is that difference only $15.84 when the room difference was $32.84?

Because I included a $17 Clark/Lake-to-Hampton car in the Hampton transportation estimate but treated the group hotel as walkable from Grand. On a lodging-only basis, the group hotel is indeed $32.84 more. If you also walk from Grand to the Hampton, its total falls to $893.62, and the full difference returns to $32.84. The Hampton is about a 12-minute walk from Grand, compared with about six minutes for the group hotel.

Got it. Keep the short car in the Hampton estimate. I do not want to walk twelve minutes alone with luggage that late. Between Tuesday-Hampton and Wednesday-Hampton, what would you choose based on the schedule?

Tuesday-Hampton is the sturdier work itinerary. It costs $265.81 more when both use the same $22 inbound and $55 outbound transportation assumptions: $910.62 versus $644.81. In return, it removes the risk of a Wednesday flight delay affecting the roundtable, gives you a full night's sleep before the meeting, and allows a normal breakfast. Wednesday morning is viable, but a delay of about 90 minutes would make the arrival tight enough that you might need to go directly to the venue with your bag.

Use Tuesday through Thursday with the Hampton. The $15.84 premium for the group hotel after realistic transportation still is not buying much, and I am fine with the Thursday morning walk. Please give me the exact working plan and total, but do not book anything yet.

Working plan selected, with nothing booked: Tuesday nonstop DFW-ORD at 6:15 p.m., arriving 8:43 p.m.; Blue Line from O'Hare to Clark/Lake, then a short car to the Hampton, with hotel arrival estimated at 10:20 to 10:40 p.m. The Hampton is held only as the preferred option for Tuesday and Wednesday nights at $497.62 total, including breakfast and cancellation until 6:00 p.m. Monday. Walk eight to ten minutes to the convening hotel Wednesday, targeting a 12:45 p.m. arrival for the 1:30 roundtable. On Thursday, leave the Hampton around 7:35 a.m. for the 7:50 site-visit shuttle. After the 11:30 finish, retrieve your bag and take a rideshare to ORD around 3:45 p.m. for the 6:55 p.m. nonstop, arriving DFW at 9:31 p.m. Airfare is $336, hotel $497.62, and Chicago transportation is estimated at $77, for a reimbursable working total of $910.62 before meals and Dallas transportation. No flight or hotel has been ticketed, held, or reserved.
